best_for: People who want a paid VPN that never asks for an email, with one flat price and up to 5 devices on one account number.
description:
Mullvad VPN is a paid VPN service from Mullvad VPN AB in Gothenburg, Sweden, which has run it since 2009. The company is fully owned by its two founders, and the desktop app is open source under the GPL-3.0.

Mullvad says it does not log what you do, and it asks outside firms to audit its apps and servers. Your DNS lookups travel inside the encrypted tunnel too. The app can block ads and trackers at the DNS level, and on Windows, split tunneling lets chosen apps skip the VPN. You get a shared IP address, not a dedicated one. Mullvad also says its obfuscation helps people get past firewalls in countries that try to block VPNs.

points.title: One price, no plans
points.text: Mullvad charges EUR 5 per month including VAT, the same whether you pay monthly or a year ahead. Crypto payments get 10% off, and there is no free tier and no sales. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: An account number instead of an email
points.text: You create an account with one click and get a number. No name or email is asked for. Cash is one of the accepted payment methods.

points.title: Refunds have a catch
points.text: There is a 14-day money-back guarantee, but cash payments are excluded under anti-money-laundering rules.

points.title: WireGuard only now
points.text: Desktop app 2025.14 dropped OpenVPN, and the OpenVPN servers were set to go offline by 15 January 2026. Router or script setups that used Mullvad's OpenVPN files stop working. For blocked networks the app offers UDP-over-TCP on port 443 and Shadowsocks.

points.title: Extra privacy layers
points.text: Multihop routes traffic through two servers in different countries, DAITA adds cover traffic against traffic analysis, and quantum-resistant tunnels can be switched on. Port forwarding was removed in May 2023.

points.title: Machine-wide install
points.text: The Windows installer installs for all users, in x64 and Arm64 builds. The Mac package is universal and needs macOS 12 or later.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 48 versions; macOS lists only the current release, so a Mac downgrade needs another source.
